dedupe_keys.name: ofgem investigation into the 9 august 2019 power outage in great britain

description: This case study is Ofgem's closed enforcement investigation into the power outage of Friday 9 August 2019 in Great Britain, together with the reports the National Grid Electricity System Operator submitted after the event. The investigation, opened in August 2019 and closed on 12 June 2020, examined the causes of the outage and the licence and code compliance of key parties. It found that the combined loss of two large generators, Hornsea One and Little Barford, which did not remain connected after a lightning strike, together with the smaller loss of generation at local level, triggered the disconnection and loss of power for more than one million consumers. Local network operators disconnected and reconnected customers as expected, except that UK Power Networks began reconnecting without being asked by the ESO. Access: the Ofgem report (PDF, 673 KB) and subsidiary ESO technical report, appendices and load disconnection report are free to download; no licence is stated. Caveats: a regulatory finding on 2019 practice, its review of the ESO's security standards was closed on administrative priority grounds, and any system data sit in the ESO technical report and appendices. It suits validation of frequency stability and cascading outage models and resilience policy evaluation, and relates to the Texas 2021 blackout case study catalogued here.
